title: About
goal: Our goal: to estimate the environmental footprint of generative AI during its use phase (inference), for the common use cases offered by the various service providers (Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, etc.), over a year of use.

existing.intro: Existing calculators offer a reading that is either:
existing.technical: technical (based on the number of tokens processed);
existing.perRequest: “per request”, which fails to reflect the volume effect of today's generative AI use, or the potential impact gap between types of use;

aims.intro: To raise awareness, this calculator therefore aims to:
aims.gaps: shed light on the impact gaps between types of use (or of request);
aims.annual: show the annual impact of a given use, for an individual or a group.

business.intro: For companies, it also aims to:
business.scale: make the impact tangible across all employees (or a group of employees), to raise awareness (as it stands, the tool is not designed to be used as an “accounting” dashboard);
business.code: put an additional focus on the use of generative AI as a coding assistant.

credits.intro: This calculator was designed by the <anchor>Green IT association</anchor>, including:

claude.title: Built with the help of Claude Code
claude.intro: The calculator's code was written with the help of <anchor>Claude Code</anchor>, Anthropic's development assistant, equipped with the association's resources:
claude.mcp: the GreenIT MCP server, which gives access to the 115 web eco-design best practices and to EcoIndex calculation;
claude.practices: the related best practices, applied at every step: eco-design of features, code writing, eco-design audit before each release.
claude.usage: From {{from}} to {{to}}, Claude (Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 models) generated {{tokens}} tokens for the team, the equivalent of {{sessions}} sessions of the “Development assistance” use case (100,000 tokens each). According to this calculator, that amounts to:
claude.limits: As in the calculator, only generated tokens are counted: tokens read as input (the project context, read again at each request) are not, which underestimates these impacts (see the <anchor>methodology's limitations</anchor>).
claude.history: Each code change states the tokens consumed and the models used: see the <anchor>project history on GitHub</anchor>.
